Class JsonExporter

java.lang.Object
ca.mcscert.jpipe.visitor.AbstractModelExporter
ca.mcscert.jpipe.visitor.JsonExporter
All Implemented Interfaces:
JustificationVisitor<Void>
public class JsonExporter extends AbstractModelExporter
Serialises a single JustificationModel to JSON text.

Uses org.json (already a declared dependency) for correct string escaping. The library is used internally as a builder; the pipeline type remains String, consistent with other text exporters (ADR-0013).

Output schema: 

{
  "name": "...",
  "type": "justification" | "template",
  "elements": [ { "type": "...", "id": "...", "label": "...",
                  "aliases": [ "..." ],
                  "origins": [ { "model": "...", "id": "...",
                                 "type": "..." }, ... ] }, ... ],
  "relations": [ { "source": "...", "target": "..." }, ... ],
  "implements": {
    "elements": [ "..." ],
    "templates": [ { "name": "...", "elements": [ "..." ],
                     "placeholders": [ { "id": "...", "label": "...",
                                         "supports": [ "..." ] } ] } ]
  }
}

The optional per-element "aliases" array lists the qualified original ids that were merged into the element during composition/unification; it is omitted for elements that are not the target of any alias. Merges compose, so the array is transitive: composing the result of a composition records a chain, and the array lists every id along it, down to those written in the original source models.

The optional per-element "origins" array is written for the elements of a model built by an operator: the elements of the models it was composed from that the element was built from, each with the name of its model, its id and its kind as the JSON export of that model writes them. It covers every level of composition, nearest first, so that an element whose kind composition changed (the hook refine merges into a sub-conclusion, the conclusion of a source assemble takes) says what it was. It is omitted for an element the operator created itself. An element inherited from a template an operator built has the origins it has in the template; a model that no operator built, and that implements no such template, has none (#200).

The optional "implements" object is written for a model that implements a template, and says how DotExporter draws it (#199). elements lists the ids drawn outside every template, in drawing order. templates lists the ancestors, the parent first, each drawn inside the one before it: its name, the ids drawn in its cluster in drawing order, and its placeholders. A placeholder is a @support filled further down the chain: its id is also in the cluster's elements, where the placeholder is drawn with its own label, and it is filled by the element of the model with the same id, drawn elsewhere. supports lists the strategies whose edge from that id is drawn from the placeholder rather than from the element filling it. The flattened elements and relations are unchanged, and never hold a placeholder.
